responsibility: This module is the core GNU Modula-2 front end and its companion support tools: it implements the multi-pass compilation pipeline that preprocesses source, lexes and buffers tokens, reparses the program through staged grammar-driven passes to discover module structure, build scopes and symbols, construct detailed types and constants, and finally emit a front-end quadruple IR that is optimized, checked, and lowered into GCC trees. Its major file families show the full subsystem boundary: `P0*`/`P1*`/`P2*`/`PC*`/`P3*` grammar and symbol-builder files drive successive syntax, declaration, constant-resolution, and executable-code passes; `SymbolTable`, `NameKey`, `SymbolKey`, `Sets`, `Lists`, and stack/queue helpers provide the compiler’s core data structures; `M2Base`, `M2System`, `M2Bitset`, `M2Size`, `M2Check`, `M2CaseList`, `M2StateCheck`, and `M2SymInit` enforce Modula-2 language rules, builtins, typing, range and initialization checks; `M2Quads`, `M2BasicBlock`, `M2Scope`, `M2SSA`, `M2Optimize`, `M2ALU`, `M2GCCDeclare`, `M2GenGCC`, and `M2Code` form the IR, analysis, declaration, and GCC-lowering path; and `M2Error`, `M2MetaError`, `M2Emit`, `M2LexBuf`, `M2Reserved`, `M2Options`, `M2Search`, `M2Batch`, `M2Scaffold`, `M2Swig`, and related utilities handle diagnostics, source locations, option/path management, module scheduling, startup scaffolding, and optional interface or dump generation. Distinct from neighboring GCC modules, this directory therefore owns nearly the entire language-specific implementation of gm2, from parsing and semantic analysis through front-end optimization and GCC tree emission, plus supporting lexer/parser-generator and link-order helper programs used by the Modula-2 toolchain.
